correction: The stated equality 1-exp(-t-t^2/2) is the n->infinity Gaussian hard-edge limit, not an exact finite-n law. At n=1 the exact CDF is erf(t/sqrt(2)), with slope sqrt(2/pi). SSS arXiv:2405.20308v2 Theorem 1.1 now gives 1+O((log n)^(-1/16)) uniformly over epsilon>=0; exact one is not concluded.
